subject: QBR sprint checkpoint: GPU runway & infra unit-econ summary
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: QBR infra checkpoint — GPU runway, batching & cache

Team —

Attaching an initial QBR checkpoint pack (spreadsheet + lightweight model) for the infra section. Goal is a concise slide + appendix we can hand to execs showing: runway (months of committed/spot capacity), unit-econ sensitivity to utilization, and the impact of batching/prefix-KV caching on effective token costs.

Key asks:
- Can each of you review the three scenarios on tab "Runway" (Conservative / Base / Aggressive) and flag any gross errors?
- Lauren: please add the OKR ask we want to call out (target runway, acceptable avg P50 latency change, and batching adoption goal).
- Vivek: sanity-check the contract/discount assumptions on tab "Pricing" (we currently assume 20% reserved discount on Dedicated).
- Marcus: can you add the FY forecasts for known enterprise commitments under deal D-4821?

Short notes on methodology: the model uses 3 utilization levers (avg GPU utilization, batching factor, prefix cache hit rate). Page "Sensitivity" runs 3x3 sweeps. Early observations: moving from 40% -> 55% utilization reduces per-token infra cost by ~18% in the Base model; adding prefix cache at 25% hit rate compounds savings but we need validation on cacheable prefix distribution from Product.

Timing: I want to lock a one-hour QBR infra dry-run on Jul 14 (afternoon PT) — propose 2:00pm PT. If that works I will circulate a 6-slide pack and the short appendix.

Attachments: 2028_Q3_gpu_runway.xlsx (model), prefix_cache_model_v2.csv (sample distribution), qbr-asklist-compact.pdf (working slides).

Karthik
Director, Infra Economics
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: QBR infra checkpoint — GPU runway, batching & cache

Thanks Karthik — this is a solid start.

Quick notes inline:
- Runway scenarios: please add a short column that calls out which business signals drive the Aggressive case (e.g., new hosted partnerships, paid pilot conversions). Execs like to see levers not just numbers.
- OKR ask (I will edit the deck): call out a target to increase effective utilization to 50% by EoQ and a batching adoption OKR that targets 30% of eligible requests. Keep the latency SLO caveat: P95 increase must be < +15% for priority routes.
- Batching vs cache: create a one-row summary that shows independent and combined effects (e.g., 40% util + no cache baseline -> 55% util + 25% cache -> savings %). It helps the story.

Meeting: 2:00pm PT on Jul 14 works for me. I'll forward calendar invite once time is locked.

-Lauren
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: QBR infra checkpoint — GPU runway, batching & cache

+1 on the structure. A few concrete asks from my side:

- Prioritize Scenario: Base+Efficiency (label it Scenario B+) — I want to show the board that small utilization improvements buy us runway while preserving margin.
- Contract assumptions: 20% reserved discount is reasonable for now but add a sensitivity at 30% — tiltcloud procurement often negotiates tiered discounts once commit thresholds hit.
- Utilization sensitivity: please include columns for +10/+20/+30% relative utilization so we can show both downside and upside to the plan.

Marcus: can you drop a short line about predictable spend from D-4821 (monthly committed GPU hours) so we can place that under the committed capacity line item?

Vivek
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: QBR infra checkpoint — GPU runway, batching & cache

Karthik —

Dropping the D-4821 numbers here: committed monthly GPU hours (approx): 42k hours/month. Billing cadence is monthly; procurement is targeting a 25% reservation once we sign the final SOW (so update the Pricing tab to show committed capacity at that cadence). Also, include a small line that shows a downside case where they delay ramp by 2 months — it materially impacts runway in the Conservative scenario.

I also uploaded a short CSV of observed prefix cacheable share from last quarter to the Drive folder (prefix_cache_model_v2.csv). It looks like sample hit rate sits around 18% on average but with long-tail customers that can push to 30% for particular workloads.

-Marcus
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Sana Rao <sana@acme.ai>
Date: 2028-07-14T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Finalized pack + dry-run invite (Jul 14, 2:00pm PT)

Folks —

Thanks for the rapid turn. Per comments I made the following changes and uploaded the updated files to the Drive link below:

- Added Scenario B+ (small utilization uplift play) and the requested +10/+20/+30% utilization columns on the Sensitivity tab.
- Pricing: added 25% reservation case and a 30% discount sensitivity.
- Runway tab: annotated business drivers for Aggressive case and a 2-month delay downside column.
- Appendix: one-page math for combined batching + prefix-cache effects (independent vs combined).

Attachments: 2028_Q3_gpu_runway.xlsx, prefix_cache_model_v2.csv, qbr-asklist-compact.pdf.

Dry-run: Jul 14, 2:00pm PT. Calendar invite sent (meeting link in the calendar). Please join with the deck loaded; I will run slides and we will aim for a 12-minute run + 30-minute Q/A.

Next steps (owners):
- Lauren: finalize OKR bullets in slide 3 and confirm latency caveat phrasing. (Due: EOD Jul 14)
- Vivek: finalize contract sensitivity language for the one-pager. (Due: EOD Jul 14)
- Marcus: send an exact committed GPU hour number for D-4821 (if you can pull the SOW sketch into the Drive folder that helps). (Due: EOD Jul 14)

I'll consolidate all final artifacts after the dry-run and push to the QBR folder.

Karthik
Director, Infra Economics
Redwood Inference
